projects/card-enjoy-now.body:
Information Desk gathers healthcare news where tech meets business, so my first round of research happens in one place.

## What it tracks
- Funding and M&A
- Papers: NEJM, JAMA, Nature Medicine and Lancet Digital Health
- Policy: FDA and CMS moves
- Investor takes and industry news
- Freshness: every story shows how old it is

## Why I built it
I pull together credible sources so I can tell my 3.5K+ LinkedIn followers what's trending and relevant in healthcare. My focus is one thing: how healthcare and technology must come together with patients and clinicians at the centre.

## How it works
- It runs entirely on GitHub, for free.
- Once an hour, a GitHub Action pulls about 30 sources, scores and de-duplicates the stories, and saves them.
- GitHub Pages serves the dashboard, which checks for new stories every 10 minutes.

projects/card-listen-heart.body:
A playbook for cold LinkedIn messages that turn into coffee chats, built over four months of messaging and reworking.

## Results
- Conversion: ~30% of cold DMs became coffee chats
- Replies: 90% from people whose work genuinely overlapped with mine

## What makes it work
Research comes first. I spent 10–15 minutes on each person's background, and dropped anyone whose work didn't connect to my experience or ambitions.

## What's inside
- A three-sentence formula
- What to cut
- Accuracy rules
- An editing loop
- Follow-ups

It also works as a Claude skill.

As a research assistant at the Center for Global Digital Health Innovation (May to July 2025), I produced two issues of its Research Roundup newsletter and ran its social media.

## This issue
Digital Health Transformation through Private Sector Engagement looks at how governments can partner with private tech companies to strengthen primary health care, drawing on the Digital Health Exemplars study of ten countries. It covers:
- How these partnerships are set up
- What makes companies take part
- How they are paid for
- Risks to manage: data privacy, vendor lock-in and regulatory oversight

projects/card-sun-will-rise.body:
I did this work as my practicum at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health's International Vaccine Access Center (IVAC).

## How I got here
I met Dr. Maria Knoll, Director of Epidemiology at IVAC, at a seminar where she presented her work with the PCV vaccine in Nepal. After a lot of pestering and follow-ups, I started working with her as a research assistant in 2024. I abstracted scientific information on the PCV vaccine in Covidence for a meta-analysis behind the WHO's immunization schedule recommendations.

## This project
- Collaboration: Severity of Pertussis in Early Infancy was my second project with her.
- My role: the quantitative data analysis for this Gates Foundation-funded project estimating pertussis-related deaths globally.

sections.body: My second contribution to this study was evaluating critical gaps in WHO pertussis mortality data in 23 countries, that earned me a first-author poster acceptance at ISPPD’26.

sections.body:
## Product and Growth
I ground Ariadne's product-market fit in patient evidence. I benchmark Komodo Health, IQVIA and Semalytix, and adapt and build onto their user interface for our product. I turn research into product decisions, build our CEO's founder brand on LinkedIn, and represent Ariadne at NYC health tech events.

## Fundraising
I run Ariadne's fundraising engine. I build and refine our 10-slide deck around one claim: we know why patients stop their medication. I position the opportunity as a $788M medication non-adherence market, with opioids as our beachhead. I manage a pipeline of 45+ investors, accelerators and grants, lead applications for fundraising, and maintain a reusable answer bank for every new program.

## Operations
I run the operating system for our three-person founding team. I keep one tracker that holds every task, owner and deadline, 65+ pharma contacts and 120+ files. I turn every team call into dated, owned action items and follow through with the team till completion. Our CEO calls it "easily the most valuable document we have."

projects/card-slow-down.body:
When I was younger, my teachers called me Miss Question Mark because my hand was always up. I wanted to know what was happening behind closed doors and which wheels were turning, and honestly, that curiosity is what got me here.

I'm a dentist by training. During dental school, I ran mobile dental camps across 48 rural sites in India and treated over 1,000 patients. I kept seeing patients whose outcomes didn't match others with the same problem who were being treated in a different setting. Why is this patient taking longer to heal? Why did that one stop showing up? Is this particular behavior happening at scale? Those weren't questions I could answer from the chair.

So I went to Johns Hopkins for my MSPH. I took courses in data science, digital health and vaccines, and learned the exact skill set to answer questions like these. For my practicum at IVAC, I did a secondary data analysis uncovering how much pertussis infection was hiding in infants and how severe it really gets. That work fed into a recommendation to the World Health Organisation. For my thesis, I built the first unified benchmark dataset for training AI models on images of the mouth: around 18,000 images across nine disease classes.

Along the way, I've always loved taking what I know and putting it into products that actually reach people. I worked in marketing for digital health startups in India, founded my own startup, Dysa.AI, at Hopkins, and now lead go-to-market and operations at another. 

Next, I want to bring all of this to breaking down the big healthcare problems. My sole motive is to keep the solutions to the problems central to two people - the person whose health is on the line and the clinician who is responsible for that.

Off the clock, I'm the eldest of three siblings, so I was born a leader. I'm also a big-time yapper. I love being on stage, whether that's hosting Hopkins' Bloomberg's Got Talent for 300+ people or moderating a conference, and making everyone in the room feel part of what's happening. And every other day, you'll find me doing yoga on a video call with my mom and my sister.

sections.heading: The vampire teeth story
sections.subtitle: How two patients turned into a study, a 1st place and a change in outreach
sections.body:
Two young patients came into my clinic in excruciating pain. They had filed their own canines into vampire fangs after a TikTok trend. I restored their teeth, but I couldn't stop thinking about it. Two cases isn't data, but I was fairly sure it wasn't a one-off.

- Flagged it: I took it to the public health department. They didn't have the funding to look into it.
- Studied it myself: I surveyed 300+ dentists across 5 dental colleges in Karnataka, and scored popular oral health videos on a validated scale. Most of the high-engagement videos weren't clinically accurate.
- Presented it: "Don't Do It Yourself: Dangers of DIY Dentistry" won the overall best e-poster, 1st out of 150+, at the first ADAI national conference in Mangalore, February 2023.

sections.heading: Why it brought me to public health
sections.subtitle: The questions I couldn't answer from the chair
sections.body:
Treating those two patients fixed two mouths. Finding out how many others were doing the same thing, and why, took a survey, a scoring scale and a room full of dentists. That was the first time I saw a problem in my clinic as a pattern in a population.

After that, I kept noticing the questions I couldn't answer from the chair. Why is this patient taking longer to heal? Why did that one stop showing up? Is this happening at scale? Public health is where those questions get answered, so I went to Johns Hopkins for my MSPH to learn how.

sections.heading: Research
sections.subtitle: Four research roles across the school
sections.body:
- International Vaccine Access Center (2025): pertussis severity in infants, and a database for the meta-analysis behind the WHO's immunization schedule recommendations. See the Pertussis in early infancy pin.
- Institute for Global Tobacco Control (Dec 2024 to Jun 2025): designed a scalable coding framework for a systematic review of tobacco-related media in 147 countries, to give global health policy an evidence base.
- Center for Global Digital Health Innovation (May to Jul 2025): produced two issues of the Research Roundup newsletter and ran the center's social media. See the Top content pin.
- GHRSTA Scholar, Gupta-Klinsky India Institute (Dec 2025 to May 2026): awarded $3,500 through the Girish and Himangi Rishi Award to define research questions for designing the India RISE Fellowship, which helps women in STEM move into leadership roles in academia.

sections.heading: Thesis

sections.body: There was no clean dataset to start from, so I built one: around 18,000 images of the mouth across nine disease classes, pulled together from scattered public sources so AI models for dental diagnostics can finally be trained and compared on the same ground. See the Screening Without Walls pin.
